t: In the Roman Republic a dictator was a lawful magistrate given supreme power for a single emergency and expected to lay it down as soon as the task was done.
Modern dictatorship, from Napoleon and the caudillos to Mussolini, Hitler and Stalin, means power held without legal limits or free elections and kept by repression and propaganda.
Political scientists divide dictatorships into personalist, military and one-party regimes, which differ in how they rule, how long they last and how they end.
dyk: The title once carried honour: Giuseppe Garibaldi officially styled himself “Dictator” of Sicily during the Expedition of the Thousand in 1860, and leaders of Poland’s November Uprising of 1830 and January Uprising of 1863 held the same title.
ev: By Roman tradition Titus Larcius is named the first dictator of the Republic
Julius Caesar is made dictator for life and assassinated; the office is then abolished
Napoleon Bonaparte seizes power in the coup of 18 Brumaire, the model of Bonapartism
The Bolsheviks take power in Russia, proclaiming a dictatorship of the proletariat
Benito Mussolini comes to power in Italy and from 1925 builds the first fascist dictatorship
Adolf Hitler becomes chancellor; the Enabling Act lets his cabinet make laws without the Reichstag
General Augusto Pinochet’s coup overthrows Chile’s elected government
Revolutions end the communist dictatorships of Central and Eastern Europe

f.power: A dictator, or in military and one-party regimes a junta or party leadership, ruling through an inner circle of officers, officials, relatives and allies; legislatures and courts are subordinate
f.legitimacy: Claimed from emergency, revolution, national salvation or ideology, often dressed in constitutions and uncompetitive elections; in Rome, a lawful appointment for a single task
f.chosen: Power taken by coup, revolution, foreign backing or an elected leader’s self-coup; lost through death, coup, revolt, defeat or negotiated transition; in Rome named by a consul
f.examples: Roman Republic under Sulla and Julius Caesar, Fascist Italy under Benito Mussolini, Nazi Germany under Adolf Hitler, Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin, Spain under Francisco Franco, Chile under Augusto Pinochet
